messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer 'acme-eu' started getting 401s after we rotated their API key in EU-prod at ~08:12 UTC. They say it affects the proxy edge only, origin requests succeed with the new key. stack: redwood-hosted API behind CDN + edge proxy.

maria: Which key did we rotate? service account or user apikey? any request ids from the customer?

alex: We rotated the service apikey bound to acme-eu-service-01 (KMS rewrap). Customer provided a sample curl and logs:

alex: ```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_OLDKEY" https://api.eu.redwood.ai/v1/generate
> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
> {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```

alex: They also forwarded an edge log snippet showing the edge rejected the old key but the origin accepted the new key: 

alex: ````
[edge-proxy] 2026-02-12T08:13:02Z req=abcd1234 auth=sk_live_OLDKEY result=invalid_api_key cache=HIT
[origin] 2026-02-12T08:13:03Z req=abcd1234 auth=sk_live_NEWKEY result=ok
````

devon: Hmm sounds like the CDN/edge still had the old key cached somewhere. We've seen this when helm chart template put the apikey into a configmap and sidecars didn't restart. Did we roll the sidecars?

jen: Confirming — the sidecar agent reads API_KEY from env at start, not hot-reload. If helm did a secret-only update without a pod restart we get a gap. I can check rollout history for the acme namespace.

maria: Customer says they restarted their app pod and still saw 401s for ~3 minutes then errors stopped. They tried a curl with the new key and it worked after ~08:16 UTC. That timing smells like CDN edge TTL.

devon: Can we verify CDN purge timeline? I see a cache-control at edge TTL=180s for auth checks. If the key used as part of auth cache key changed, some edge nodes might still have cached auth result. We should have an explicit cache-busting header during rotation.

sam: Also double-check Vault/KMS rewrap: sometimes the key alias mismatch leads to the access token being accepted by origin due to forwarded header rewrite but edge uses a different verification path. Run: 

sam: ```bash
# check vault path and latest version
vault kv get -field=api_key secret/acme-eu/service || true
# verify kms alias used for rewrap
aws kms list-aliases --region eu-west-1 | grep acme-eu-rewrap || true
```

jen: I pulled the acme namespace rollout: last helm upgrade updated secret only (kubectl apply --record). No pod restart triggered. Sidecars still running old env. That matches.

alex: Customer's support ticket shows they used a hosted Lambda which also had a cached connection pool to the edge — connections reused old token in proxy auth header for a bit.

maria: Immediate remediation steps we did with customer: 1) Purged CDN edge keys for acme-eu prefix, 2) asked them to restart pods (or do a rolling restart), 3) forced sidecar restart.

devon: Commands we suggested: 

devon: ```bash
# purge edge cache for service prefix
redwood-edgectl purge --prefix /v1/acme-eu/ --region eu
# force kubernetes rollout restart
kubectl -n acme rollout restart deployment/acme-service
```

alex: deploy-bot: deploy acme-eu-service rollback performed at 2026-02-12T08:15:10Z - status: success.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: rollback completed (release v42 -> v41)

maria: After purge + restarts customer reported requests good again at 08:16:45 UTC. They saw brief token mismatch windows for ~3m consistent with edge TTL. Customer asked for follow-up: can we make rotation smoother so there is no 401 window?

sam: Long term: implement coordinated rotation flow — 1) publish new key to origin and consumers, 2) invalidate edge auth cache explicitly, 3) sweep any connection pools (recommend client keep-alive reestablish). Also update our rotation runbook to include a CDN purge step and to trigger pod rolling restarts when secrets change.

jen: I'll add a k8s post-update hook in the helm chart to annotate deployments so secrets updates cause a restart. Also file a tiny infra task to add an edge cache-bust API call in the rotation orchestration.

maria: I'll send the customer a postmortem note describing root cause and mitigation steps. They were fine with rollback + restart but asked for a fix. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks team. Logging follow-up: please add an alert if >5% 401 spikes in a 5m window after a rotation event. That will help catch this earlier.

devon: Added to triage board. I'll submit the infra PR tomorrow.

maria: closing this support thread with the customer — thanks everyone.

sam: quick note: security reviewed rollback flow, no creds exposed in logs. all good.

alex: resolved — marking customer ticket as 'resolved' and linking to new runbook entry.
